numberItems.stem: A roadside test measures a CMV driver's blood alcohol concentration (BAC). At what level is it illegal to drive the CMV?
numberItems.explanation: It is illegal to operate a CMV with a BAC of .04 percent or more (p. 1-14). .08 is the familiar car limit.

numberItems.stem: You are driving a CMV and a test shows a BAC of .03. What happens?
options: You lose your CDL for at least 1 year
You lose your CDL for at least 60 days
You are put out of service for 24 hours
numberItems.explanation: Any detectable alcohol under .04 puts you out of service for 24 hours (p. 1-14); 1 year is the penalty at .04 or more.

numberItems.stem: First offense: you leave the scene of an accident while driving a CMV **placarded for hazardous materials**. You lose your CDL for at least:
numberItems.explanation: A first major offense costs at least 1 year, but at least 3 years if it happens in a CMV placarded for HazMat; life is for a second offense (p. 1-14).

numberItems.stem: A driver uses a CMV to commit a felony involving controlled substances. It is the driver's first offense. How long is the CDL lost?
numberItems.explanation: Using a CMV to commit a felony involving controlled substances costs the CDL for life, even the first time (p. 1-14).

numberItems.stem: Which speed counts as "excessive speeding," a serious traffic violation?
options: 10 mph or more over the posted limit
15 mph or more over the posted limit
Any amount over the posted limit
numberItems.explanation: Excessive speeding is 15 mph or more above the posted limit (p. 1-14).

numberItems.stem: You are convicted of your third serious traffic violation in a CMV within 3 years. You lose your CDL for at least:
numberItems.explanation: 3 or more serious traffic violations within 3 years in a CMV cost the CDL for at least 120 days; 2 cost at least 60 days (p. 1-14).

numberItems.stem: You violate an out-of-service order for the second time in 10 years. Under the California handbook, you lose your CDL for at least:
numberItems.explanation: Handbook: 90 days for a first out-of-service violation, 1 year for 2 in 10 years, 3 years for 3 or more (p. 1-14). 2 years is the federal figure.

numberItems.stem: A CMV driver is convicted of a **first** railroad-highway grade crossing violation. What is the penalty?
options: No disqualification until a second violation
CDL lost for at least 60 days
CDL lost for at least 90 days
numberItems.explanation: A first railroad crossing violation costs the CDL for at least 60 days (p. 1-14); unlike serious violations, a first one already counts.

numberItems.stem: How many railroad-highway grade crossing offenses does the handbook list as grounds for disqualification?
numberItems.explanation: The handbook lists 6 offenses at railroad-highway grade crossings (pp. 1-14 to 1-15).

numberItems.stem: Your car license was suspended once for DUI. Now you are convicted of a second alcohol violation, this time in a CMV. How long do you lose your CDL?
numberItems.explanation: A car suspension for alcohol, drugs or a felony costs the CDL for 1 year; a second such violation, in your car or a CMV, costs it for life (p. 1-15).

numberItems.stem: [CA] How long do out-of-service violations stay on a CDL holder's driving record?
numberItems.explanation: Out-of-service violations are kept 15 years; major violations 55, accidents and serious violations 10, railroad 4, minor convictions 3 (p. 1-15).

numberItems.stem: [CA] You are convicted of a 2-point violation while driving a CMV. How does it count on your record?
options: The same as in a car: 2 points
numberItems.explanation: A violation received in a CMV carries 1½ times the point count, so 2 points become 3 (p. 1-15).

numberItems.stem: [CA] What is the lowest point count within **24 months** that makes a CMV driver a negligent operator?
numberItems.explanation: Negligent operator: 4 points in 12 months, 6 in 24 months, or 8 in 36 months (p. 1-15).

numberItems.stem: [CA] If you request and appear for a hearing, and the points were not earned in a noncommercial Class C vehicle, the negligent-operator counts may be raised to:
options: Any number, as long as the points were earned in a Class C car
numberItems.explanation: After a hearing you may be allowed a higher count of 6, 8 or 10 points, if the 4, 6 or 8 points were not obtained in a noncommercial Class C vehicle (p. 1-15).

numberItems.stem: [CA] A Class A or B driver who has no special certificate or endorsement may be allowed how many additional points before being called a negligent operator?
numberItems.explanation: A Class A or B driver without a special certificate or endorsement may be allowed 2 additional points (p. 1-15).

numberItems.stem: [CA] You get your **third** hands-free or texting violation within 3 years. What happens to your CDL?
options: Lost for at least 60 days, plus 1 point
Lost for at least 120 days, plus 1 point
Lost for at least 1 year, plus 1 point
numberItems.explanation: Third and later hands-free/texting violations within 3 years cost the CDL for at least 120 days plus 1 point; the second costs 60 days plus 1 point (p. 1-16).
